$schema: The Datum family registry. One entry per app; the hub site reads each repo's docs/site.json, CHANGELOG.md and latest release when it builds. A branch of HEAD follows the repo's default branch. The name, accent, tagline, for and shot (one screenshot) fields here are only used until the app publishes docs/site.json. An optional status field (Stable, Beta, Alpha) overrides the badge worked out from the version. The about (paragraphs) and steps (how the app is used: title and text) fields fill the app's page on the site; site.json can set its own.

apps.name: Datum Plan
apps.tagline: Plan, schedule, track and report projects.
apps.for: Project managers, planners, engineers and contractors.
about: Datum Plan is a desktop scheduler for project managers, planners, engineers and contractors. You enter tasks in a sheet that works like a spreadsheet, link them, and the engine works out the critical path to the minute, with working calendars, constraints, every link type and resource levelling.

As the work goes on, you record progress and actuals against up to 11 baselines and see where the project stands: a tracking Gantt, earned value, S-curves, a dashboard and progress reports. Plans open from common scheduling files (XML, XER, MPX), export to Excel with formulas, and every view prints to PDF.

steps.title: Enter the tasks
steps.text: Type tasks, durations and resources into the sheet, or open an existing plan.

steps.title: Link and schedule
steps.text: Link the tasks; the engine works out dates, float and the critical path.

steps.title: Track and report
steps.text: Save a baseline, record progress, and print the Gantt, the S-curve and the reports.

apps.name: Datum Plot
apps.tagline: Analyse data and make publication-ready graphs.
apps.for: Scientists, researchers, lab teams and students.
about: Datum Plot keeps data, analyses and graphs linked. Type or paste data into a table, choose an analysis, and the results and the graph follow; change a value and everything updates.

It covers the statistics most lab and research work needs, from t-tests and ANOVA to regression and curve fitting, explains each result in plain words with ready methods text, and makes figures ready for a journal: multi-panel layouts at journal sizes, exported as PNG, TIFF, SVG, PDF or EPS. Python runs inside the app, with nothing else to install.

steps.title: Enter the data
steps.text: Choose a table for your kind of data and type, paste or import it.

steps.title: Analyse
steps.text: Pick a test or a fit; results, P values and the methods text appear beside the data.

steps.title: Graph and export
steps.text: Style the graph, lay out the figure and export it at journal size.

apps.name: Datum Atlas
apps.tagline: Choose materials with property charts and selection indices.
apps.for: Design and materials engineers, and students.
about: Datum Atlas helps you pick a material and show why it is the right one. Choose a design goal, such as a light, stiff beam or a cheap, strong tie, and Atlas sets the property chart, the selection line and the limits for you.

Every material is a bubble spanning its range of values, grouped by family. Limits, index lines and boxes narrow the field; the materials that pass are ranked, and every one that fails says why. Every value names its public source, and you can add your own materials.

steps.title: Pick a goal
steps.text: Choose a design goal, or set the two properties to chart yourself.

steps.title: Chart and select
steps.text: Move the selection line, add limits and boxes, and watch the field narrow.

steps.title: Rank and report
steps.text: Compare the materials that pass, open their datasheets, and print or export the result.

apps.name: Datum Sim
apps.tagline: Model and simulate dynamic systems: block diagrams, control and motors.
apps.for: Control, mechanical, electrical, process and mechatronics engineers, researchers and students.
about: Datum Sim models and simulates dynamic systems. You draw the system as blocks and wires: sources, transfer functions, state space, PID controllers, motors and lookup tables. Then press Run and watch the signals on live scopes.

Five solvers cover everything from simple fixed-step runs to stiff systems with exact switching times. Parameter sweeps, step-response specifications and Bode plots come from a built-in Python engine, and every block and solver is checked against known answers.

steps.title: Draw the model
steps.text: Drag blocks from the library, wire them together and set their parameters.

steps.title: Run
steps.text: Choose a solver and a stop time, press Run and watch the scopes live.

steps.title: Analyse and tune
steps.text: Sweep parameters, read the step-response specifications and tune the controller.
